feedback:
Approved because this is the last action run this iteration, so a revise round cannot be raced. Iteration 0 is the only evidence: all 60 trials went off_track with zero finishes, max_error sat at 0.062 to 0.064 (just past the 0.06 m limit) while rms_error stayed at 0.02 to 0.03, and line_loss_events were 1 to 2 per run. The failure is edge recovery on bends, not average tracking, and the proposed kp 2.5 to 3.5 targets that directly. The candidate's controller-only change keeps geometry fixed, which isolates the controller effect. I cannot say how it will perform; the race will show it.

Risk to watch: base_speed 1.6 to 1.4 lowers average speed. The contract needs roughly 1.5 m/s to finish in 3 s, so completion may become impossible even if the robot stays on the line. Judge the next iteration from the telemetry as follows. If max_error is still at or above 0.06 with the robot leaving the line, the limit is speed or recovery, so drop base_speed further in small steps. If the robot stays on the line (max_error below 0.06, line_loss_events near 0) but completion_time exceeds 3 s, raise base_speed in steps of about 0.1 while watching max_error. If steering_oscillation rises sharply with kp 3.5, kd is too low for the gain, so raise kd from 0.4 toward 0.6.
requested_changes: If the next race shows max_error still at or above 0.06 with off_track endings, reduce controller.base_speed below 1.4 (for example 1.2) to test whether speed is the limit, since iteration 0 max_error sat at 0.062 to 0.064 at base_speed 1.6.

If the robot stays on the line (max_error below 0.06, line_loss_events near 0) but completion_time exceeds 3 s, raise controller.base_speed in steps of about 0.1 (1.4 to 1.5 to 1.6), because the contract needs about 1.5 m/s average to finish.
If steering_oscillation rises sharply with kp 3.5 (iteration 0 was 0.11 to 0.15), raise controller.kd from 0.4 toward 0.6 to damp the higher gain, keeping kp at 3.5.
